subject: Business
title: Single Sourcing vs. Multi-Sourcing
description: A quick, practical guide to Single Sourcing vs. Multi-Sourcing.

hook.text: Your sole supplier's factory floods. Production stops. You have zero alternatives. Revenue drops to zero.

buildup.text: Single sourcing means relying on one supplier for a component. Multi-sourcing spreads risk across several.

discovery.text: Single sourcing gives better prices and stronger relationships. Multi-sourcing provides backup and leverage.

twist.text: After COVID, companies that single-sourced from China scrambled to find alternatives. Diversification became urgent.

climax.text: Apple dual-sources critical chips from TSMC and Samsung to ensure no single failure stops iPhone production.

punchline.text: One supplier is efficient. Two suppliers is insurance.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of single sourcing?
options: One supplier failure can halt your entire production
Single sources always charge higher prices

details.summary: Single sourcing relies on one supplier for a component while multi-sourcing splits orders among several. Single sourcing offers volume discounts and simpler management but creates vulnerability. Multi-sourcing provides resilience but increases complexity and may reduce economies of scale.
details.whyItMatters: The sourcing strategy directly determines supply chain risk exposure. Single-source dependencies have caused major production shutdowns when suppliers fail. The tradeoff between efficiency and resilience is a critical strategic decision.
takeaways: Single sourcing maximizes volume leverage but creates dependency risk
Multi-sourcing builds resilience through redundancy at higher complexity cost
Dual sourcing is a common compromise balancing efficiency and risk mitigation

faq.question: When does single sourcing make strategic sense?
faq.answer: When the component requires specialized capabilities only one supplier has, when volume concentration yields significant cost advantages, when quality consistency demands deep partner investment, or when the component has low supply risk due to commodity availability.

faq.question: How does dual sourcing balance the tradeoffs?
faq.answer: Dual sourcing typically splits volume 70-30 between a primary and backup supplier. The primary gets enough volume for competitive pricing while the backup maintains capability and readiness. If the primary fails, the backup can ramp up to cover demand.
